events.title: Napoleon survives a bomb in the rue Saint-Nicaise
events.description: Royalist plotters exploded a barrel bomb in a Paris street as the First Consul's carriage passed, killing several bystanders but missing Napoleon. He used the attack to deport Jacobin opponents.
events.html: Royalist plotters exploded a barrel bomb in a Paris street as the First Consul's carriage passed, killing several bystanders but missing Napoleon. He used the attack to deport Jacobin opponents.

events.title: The Treaty of Ghent ends the War of 1812
events.description: British and American negotiators signed a peace treaty at Ghent, restoring pre-war borders. News travelled slowly, and the Battle of New Orleans was fought two weeks later.
events.html: British and American negotiators signed a peace treaty at Ghent, restoring pre-war borders. News travelled slowly, and the Battle of New Orleans was fought two weeks later.

events.title: Fire destroys much of the Library of Congress
events.description: A fire in the Capitol destroyed about 35,000 of the Library of Congress's 55,000 books, including around two-thirds of the collection bought from Thomas Jefferson in 1815.
events.html: A fire in the Capitol destroyed about 35,000 of the Library of Congress's 55,000 books, including around two-thirds of the collection bought from Thomas Jefferson in 1815.

events.title: The Christmas Truce begins on the Western Front
events.description: On Christmas Eve, soldiers along parts of the front sang carols across the lines. Over the next day many British and German troops met in no man's land, swapped gifts and buried their dead.
events.html: On Christmas Eve, soldiers along parts of the front sang carols across the lines. Over the next day many British and German troops met in no man's land, swapped gifts and buried their dead.

events.title: Apollo 8 orbits the Moon
events.description: Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders became the first people to orbit the Moon. They photographed 'Earthrise' and read from Genesis in a Christmas Eve broadcast seen by millions.
events.html: Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders became the first people to orbit the Moon. They photographed 'Earthrise' and read from Genesis in a Christmas Eve broadcast seen by millions.
